issues.label: Standard of review for procedural fairness issues
Procedural fairness complaint about tribunal record preparation
Procedural fairness complaint about admission of records as new facts
Standard of review for correctness of test selection and reasonableness of application
Whether the Member applied the correct test for leave to appeal
Effect of Member's error in test selection on judicial review remedy
Application of res judicata and issue estoppel to disability and new facts issues
Disposition of judicial review application and costs

result.overall: The Court found that the Social Security Tribunal (SST) Member erred in applying the wrong test for leave to appeal but dismissed the judicial review application because the error was harmless due to res judicata and issue estoppel preventing re-litigation of disability and new facts issues.

themes.name: Standard of review for procedural fairness issues
themes.summary: The Court considered the appropriate standard of review for procedural fairness issues raised by the Applicant.

themes.name: Procedural fairness complaint about tribunal record preparation
themes.summary: The Applicant claimed procedural unfairness due to the condition of the tribunal record, specifically unnumbered pages.

themes.name: Procedural fairness complaint about admission of records as new facts
themes.summary: The Applicant argued that refusal to admit certain medical reports as new facts breached procedural fairness.

themes.name: Standard of review for correctness of test selection and reasonableness of application
themes.summary: The Court analyzed the standard of review for whether the correct test for leave to appeal was applied and whether it was reasonably applied.

themes.name: Whether the Member applied the correct test for leave to appeal
themes.summary: The Court found the Member applied the wrong test for leave to appeal, relying on the former 'arguable case' test instead of the statutory 'reasonable chance of success' test.

themes.name: Effect of Member's error in test selection on judicial review remedy
themes.summary: The Court held that the Member's error did not warrant setting aside the decision because res judicata and issue estoppel barred re-litigation and the outcome would be the same.

themes.name: Application of res judicata and issue estoppel to disability and new facts issues
themes.summary: The Court applied res judicata and issue estoppel to bar re-litigation of the Applicant's disability status and the status of medical reports as new facts.

themes.name: Disposition of judicial review application and costs
themes.summary: The Court dismissed the judicial review application and declined to order costs against the Applicant.

arguments.quote: The Applicant argues that the SST erred in denying her application for leave to appeal.
arguments.claim: The SST erred in denying leave to appeal and should have allowed submission of new medical reports as new facts to show disability.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court found the denial reasonable and barred by res judicata.

arguments.quote: The Applicant submits that these reports raise new material facts that were not previously discoverable with reasonable diligence.
arguments.claim: The medical reports constitute new material facts justifying reopening the appeal.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court held the reports do not constitute new facts and issue estoppel applies.

arguments.quote: The Applicant pleads that there have been breaches of procedural fairness.
arguments.claim: Refusal to admit reports denied her right to a fair hearing, breaching procedural fairness.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court found no breach of procedural fairness regarding record preparation or admission of evidence.

arguments.quote: The Applicant also argues that certain information that she requested from the Minister and the Office of the Commissioner of Review Tribunals was not produced.
arguments.claim: Failure to produce requested information and unnumbered pages in the tribunal file breached procedural fairness.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court found the unnumbered pages immaterial and no procedural fairness breach.

arguments.quote: The Respondent submits that the appropriate standard of review of the decision to deny leave to appeal is reasonableness.
arguments.claim: The decision to deny leave to appeal should be reviewed on a reasonableness standard.

arguments.quote: The Respondent argues that the issue of whether the Tribunal selected the correct test for granting leave to appeal is likewise reviewable on the standard of reasonableness.
arguments.claim: The selection of the correct test for leave to appeal is reviewable on reasonableness standard.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court held test selection is reviewable on correctness standard.
arguments.quote_snapped: [44] The Respondent then argues that the issue of whether the Tribunal selected the correct test for granting leave to appeal is likewise reviewable on the standard of reasonableness.

arguments.quote: The Respondent submits that previously, the test for leave to appeal was whether there was an “arguable case”.
arguments.claim: The former test for leave to appeal was 'arguable case'; the new test is 'reasonable chance of success' without new evidence consideration.

arguments.quote: The Respondent argues that although the Member appears to have analysed the Applicant’s application for leave based on the former test, the grounds of appeal set out in subsection 58(1) of the DHRSDA were still addressed in her decision.
arguments.claim: Despite using the old test, the Member addressed the statutory grounds of appeal.

arguments.quote: He submits that the doctrine of res judicata applies, and that the Member’s decision to deny leave was reasonable.
arguments.claim: Res judicata applies to bar re-litigation; the denial of leave was reasonable.

arguments.quote: He argues that the Applicant has failed to provide new facts that would justify re-opening the decision of the first review tribunal.
arguments.claim: Applicant failed to provide new facts to justify reopening the first tribunal decision.

arguments.quote: The Respondent submits that the Applicant does not have a reasonable chance of success in the present application because previous proceedings have already determined that the evidence presented by the Applicant... do not constitute new facts.
arguments.claim: Previous decisions that the evidence does not constitute new facts are final and bar success.

arguments.quote: The Respondent submits that the Applicant’s complaint that the third Review Tribunal did not return the tribunal file to her is an administrative complaint that is irrelevant to this application.
arguments.claim: Complaint about tribunal file handling is irrelevant and not a ground with reasonable chance of success.

arguments.quote: The Member found there was no merit to the Applicant’s argument that the Review Tribunal did not provide a complete file for the hearing.
arguments.claim: The Review Tribunal fulfilled its obligation regarding the hearing file; parties must ensure tribunal has all relevant material.

arguments.quote: The Member refused the application for leave to appeal on the basis that the Applicant had not produced any new evidence, nor pointed to an error in fact or law, nor presented any argument that would have a reasonable chance of success.
arguments.claim: Leave to appeal was refused because no new evidence, no error in fact or law, and no arguable ground was shown.

holdings.quote: Issues of procedural fairness are reviewable on the standard of correctness
holdings.statement: Procedural fairness issues are reviewed on a correctness standard.

holdings.quote: There has been no breach of procedural fairness in respect of the preparation of the tribunal record
holdings.statement: No procedural fairness breach found regarding unnumbered pages in tribunal record.

holdings.quote: The fact that the records were not admitted into the record is an issue related to the merits of the decision since those records were deemed to not constitute new facts
holdings.statement: Refusal to admit records as new facts is a merits issue, not a procedural fairness issue.

holdings.quote: The first question, that is whether the correct test was applied, is reviewable on the correctness standard
holdings.statement: Selection of the correct test for leave to appeal is reviewed on correctness standard.

holdings.quote: The second question of whether the test was properly applied is subject to review on a standard of reasonableness
holdings.statement: Application of the test is reviewed on a reasonableness standard.

holdings.quote: I do not agree with the submissions of the Respondent that the first question is reviewable on a standard of reasonableness
holdings.statement: The Court rejects that test selection is reviewable on reasonableness, affirming correctness standard.

holdings.quote: Although granting or refusing leave to appeal involves an interpretation of the SST’s home statute, the question of whether the correct test was selected by the Member only has two possible outcomes
holdings.statement: Correct test selection is a binary question suitable for correctness review to avoid uncertainty.

holdings.quote: In my opinion, she did not [select the correct test]
holdings.statement: The Member erred in selecting the correct test for leave to appeal.
holdings.quote_snapped: In my opinion, she did not.

holdings.quote: The Member erred when she considered the Applicant’s leave application on the basis of her expectations at the time of filing her application for leave to appeal
holdings.statement: The Member wrongly applied the former test based on Applicant's legitimate expectations rather than the statutory test.

holdings.quote: The test under the former regime was one developed by the jurisprudence, that is, at common law
holdings.statement: Former test for leave to appeal was 'arguable case' including new evidence consideration.

holdings.quote: The test for obtaining leave to appeal has changed
holdings.statement: The statutory test under DHRSDA is 'reasonable chance of success' with enumerated grounds of appeal excluding new evidence.

holdings.quote: The use of the word “only” in subsection 58(1) of the DHRSDA means that no other grounds of appeal may be considered
holdings.statement: The statutory grounds of appeal are exclusive and limit the basis for leave to appeal.

holdings.quote: Adducing new evidence is no longer a ground of appeal, and the Member erred in considering it as such
holdings.statement: New evidence is not a ground for leave to appeal under current legislation; Member erred by considering it.

holdings.quote: The Member was required to apply the test set out in section 58 of the DHRSDA
holdings.statement: The Member had no discretion to apply the former test and erred by doing so.

holdings.quote: The doctrine of legitimate expectations is an aspect of procedural fairness and is limited to the rules of procedural fairness
holdings.statement: Legitimate expectations doctrine does not create substantive rights or preserve old law in this context.

holdings.quote: No one has a vested right to continuance of the law as it stood in the past
holdings.statement: Applicants cannot expect the law to remain unchanged over time.

holdings.quote: The transitional provisions... make it clear that Parliament intended that matters dealt with by the SST would be subject to the new legislation
holdings.statement: Transitional provisions require application of new legislation to appeals before the SST.

holdings.quote: The Member erred in assessing the Applicant’s leave application in accordance with the doctrine of legitimate expectations
holdings.statement: Applying legitimate expectations to preserve old law was erroneous.

holdings.quote: Relief in applications for judicial review is discretionary
holdings.statement: Judicial review relief is discretionary and not every legal error warrants remedy.

holdings.quote: Prerogative relief... may be refused on the ground of futility
holdings.statement: Relief may be refused if it would have no practical effect or value.

holdings.quote: Sending this matter back to the SST for re-determination will have no practical effect
holdings.statement: Remanding for correct test application would not change outcome due to res judicata.

holdings.quote: Both these issues... have already been finally decided and are subject to the evidentiary rule res judicata and the law of estoppel
holdings.statement: Disability status and new facts issues are final and barred from re-litigation.

holdings.quote: The doctrine of issue estoppel applies, and the matter is res judicata
holdings.statement: Issue estoppel bars re-litigation of disability and new facts issues in this case.

holdings.quote: The Applicant does not have a ground of appeal with a reasonable chance of success
holdings.statement: Applicant's appeal lacks a reasonable chance of success under current law.

holdings.quote: I decline to grant a remedy for the Member’s error of law and this application for judicial review is dismissed
holdings.statement: Judicial review application dismissed; no remedy granted for Member's error.

holdings.quote: I am not persuaded that costs against the Applicant are justified in this case and make no Order as to costs
holdings.statement: No costs ordered against the Applicant.
